title: Proactive Signal Library
description: Example lifecycle signals that can prompt one timely, helpful PAL conversation. These are proposed patterns, not live Tavus telemetry or enabled triggers.

signals.title: Exploring pricing or plan details
signals.trigger: A user visits the pricing or plan-comparison page multiple times in a short window, or explicitly opens a plan comparison.
signals.interpretation: The user may be evaluating capacity, price, or plan differences. Page activity alone is not confirmed buying intent.
signals.opener: Hi there, I noticed you have been exploring our plans. Are you comparing what each plan includes, or are you running into a limit? I can help you find the right fit.
signals.next_best_action: Ask what the user is trying to accomplish, answer the specific plan question, and compare options against verified usage and current plan terms.
signals.success_metric: User confirms the plan question was answered or identifies an eligible plan that fits the stated need.
signals.guardrail: Do not infer willingness to pay, create urgency, or present unverified pricing or plan limits. Offer an upgrade only when the user confirms a relevant need.

signals.title: Support ticket still open
signals.trigger: A support ticket remains unresolved beyond its expected response window, or the user revisits the same help topic while the ticket is open.
signals.interpretation: The issue may still be blocking progress; ticket status alone does not reveal urgency or whether the user already got help elsewhere.
signals.opener: Hi there, I noticed your support ticket about [topic] is still open. Is this blocking what you are trying to do? I can help route it for an update.
signals.next_best_action: Confirm the issue is still active, then offer a support escalation or status check through an approved workflow.
signals.success_metric: Support acknowledges the escalation within the target response window and the user confirms whether the blocker is resolved.
signals.guardrail: Ask before escalation when possible. Never claim a ticket was escalated, assigned, or resolved until the support system confirms it. Share only the minimum ticket context.

signals.title: Minutes over plan for three consecutive months
signals.trigger: Verified usage records show conversation minutes exceeded the included allowance in each of the last three complete billing periods.
signals.interpretation: Sustained overage may mean the workflow is growing or the current allowance no longer fits. First confirm the pattern is expected and useful.
signals.opener: Hi there, I noticed your workspace has gone over its included conversation minutes in each of the last three months. Is that steady demand, or was it a short-term spike? Do you need more room for your workflows?
signals.next_best_action: Review verified usage and the user's forecast. If more capacity is needed, explain the current plan options. A temporary 2×-minutes offer can be mentioned only if it is approved, available, and the account is eligible.
signals.success_metric: User confirms the capacity need; measure suitable plan selection or approved offer acceptance alongside retained usage, gross margin, and support/refund guardrails.
signals.guardrail: Do not equate overage with upgrade intent. Never promise doubled minutes, alter billing, or grant a promotion unless a trusted policy and system confirm the terms and eligibility.

signals.title: API or MCP connected, but no successful first use
signals.trigger: A connection or authorization succeeded, but no successful conversation or tool result is recorded within the validated observation window.
signals.interpretation: Setup progress is promising, but the user may still need help turning the connection into a useful test.
signals.opener: Hi there, I noticed the connection is set up, but I do not see a successful first test recorded yet. What were you hoping to try? I can help you get that first result.
signals.next_best_action: Guide one short, low-risk test that matches the user's stated use case and confirm whether the result was useful.
signals.success_metric: First successful conversation or tool result, followed by user-confirmed usefulness.
signals.guardrail: Check event coverage before interpreting a missing result. Do not claim the integration failed or succeeded without a reliable event.

signals.title: Repeated successful use across separate days
signals.trigger: The account completes useful conversations on multiple distinct days and returns to the same workflow or deploys it.
signals.interpretation: The workflow may be becoming habitual and could benefit from a next-step review; repeat use by itself does not mean the user wants to buy more.
signals.opener: Hi there, I noticed you have been using [workflow] regularly. What are you hoping to improve next? I can help you look at the next step.
signals.next_best_action: Ask what outcome they want next; offer a deployment, workflow optimization, or capacity review only when it matches that stated goal.
signals.success_metric: A user-confirmed next workflow milestone, sustained useful repeat use, or an explicitly requested plan review.
signals.guardrail: Do not turn engagement into an automatic upsell. Respect contact frequency limits, channel permissions, and opt-outs.
